test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In relation to the scope of economics, which of the following statements is regarded as a traditional approach and NOT modern approach?

options.text: Welfare economics and growth economics are more normative than positive.
Social problems can thus be explained by abstract theoretical tools or by empirical methods.
The scope of economics lies in analysing economic problems and suggesting policy measures.

solution:
The correct answer is** Economics is a social science.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Economics is a social science:**

 
 
• This statement reflects the traditional approach to the scope of economics. Traditionally, economics has been regarded as a social science that studies human behavior, particularly the allocation of scarce resources to meet various needs and wants.
 
• It emphasizes the study of economic activities and interactions within a society, focusing on how individuals and groups make decisions about production, distribution, and consumption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Welfare economics and growth economics are more normative than positive:**

 
 
• This statement reflects a more modern approach. Modern economics often distinguishes between positive economics (which is descriptive and based on observable phenomena) and normative economics (which involves value judgments and policy recommendations).
 
• Welfare economics and growth economics, which deal with issues like income distribution and economic development, often involve normative analysis.
 
 
 
• **Social problems can thus be explained by abstract theoretical tools or by empirical methods:**
 
 
• This statement also reflects a modern approach, emphasizing the use of both theoretical models and empirical data to analyze and solve social and economic problems.
 
• Modern economics relies heavily on quantitative methods and statistical analysis to test theories and inform policy decisions.
 
 
 
• **The scope of economics lies in analysing economic problems and suggesting policy measures:**
 
 
• This statement aligns with the modern approach, which focuses on applying economic theories and models to real-world problems and developing policy recommendations to address those problems.
 
• Modern economists often work closely with policymakers to design and evaluate economic policies aimed at improving social welfare and economic efficiency.
